name: Brisbane Multimodal Terminal
network_role: Road/rail/container-terminal interface; standard- and narrow-gauge access; interstate rail connects via Acacia Ridge
notes: Port-owned open-access interface; distinguish from Acacia Ridge inland/interstate terminal.

name: Acacia Ridge intermodal terminal
network_role: Key Brisbane interstate rail interface; Port of Brisbane rail line connects to interstate heavy rail network via QR multi-user terminal at Acacia Ridge
notes: Further ownership/capacity detail required before scoring.

name: Bromelton terminal precinct
network_role: Southern Brisbane-region freight node connected to east-coast interstate corridor; ARTC operational notices show trains passing Bromelton
notes: Need separate current terminal/operator/capacity verification; retain status cautiously.

name: Riverina Intermodal Freight and Logistics Hub
network_role: Connects to Main Southern railway; 4.6 km master siding; designed for 1800m+ trains and regional industry/freight
notes: Opened Dec 2022; Visy Logistics operates/manages terminal/master siding under PPP with Council.

name: Parkes Logistics / Goobang intermodal complex
network_role: East-west and north-south rail junction area; current ARTC train notices show Perth-Sydney services using Parkes Logistics Terminal and Goobang Junction
notes: Terminal system should later be decomposed by operator/site; Parkes is a network node, not one homogeneous terminal.

name: Moorebank Interstate Terminal
network_role: Independent open-access interstate terminal linked to Southern Sydney Freight Line; designed for 1800m trains; current four 900m tracks
notes: Opened Apr 2024; current capacity 250,000 TEU/year, expandable to 500,000 TEU/year with eight 900m tracks and gantry cranes.

name: Moorebank IMEX Terminal
network_role: Open-access import/export terminal linking Port Botany with south-west Sydney warehousing/distribution and interstate rail network
notes: Ultimate approval/contract capacity around 1.05m TEU/year; current operational capacity should be kept distinct from ultimate capacity.

name: Enfield Intermodal Logistics Centre
network_role: 60ha logistics centre 18km from Port Botany on direct dedicated freight rail; road access to Hume, M4 and M5
notes: NSW Ports states significant additional container-handling capacity and is investing $250m in the site.

name: Cooks River Intermodal Terminal
network_role: Direct daily Port Botany rail shuttles; multiple sidings can accommodate regional trains; major empty-container storage function
notes: Important near-port node; storage/service capacity should not be confused with annual intermodal throughput capacity.
